$comment: CAP: 12 prose entries across expected_shape · read_this_way · suspicious_if ·
blind_spots · decisions · review_notes · expected · known_normal · known_bad ·
The cap is checked over this file by step-validate fast invariant #45 (NOTES-CAP). When a 13th wants in
there are exactly two legal resolutions: PROMOTE it to a check, or DELETE it.
There is no overflow file and no overflow block.
`fences` and `counts` are RECORD blocks, not prose — they are not counted against
the cap. `fences` lives here because the descriptor schema's root is
additionalProperties:false and has no fences category (Spec 120 §14.0).

expected_shape.what: A healthy run of this step arrives at the tier-2 content-hash gate, not at a load. CKAN regenerates the centreline zip DAILY, so the tier-1 HTTP validators (last-modified/etag) report 'changed' on nearly every run while the bytes are identical; the normal audit table is the pre rows plus `centreline_load_skipped` with a `content_hash_unchanged`-class reason and no write counters at all. A full 47K-row staged replace is the exception, and CENTRELINE_FORCE_RELOAD=1 is how you ask for one.

read_this_way.what: `centreline_features_deleted` is the PRE-state row count of toronto_centreline, NOT churn. Every load is an unconditional whole-table DELETE followed by an INSERT…SELECT from the temp stage, so this run's `deleted` equals the PRIOR run's `inserted` whenever both were full replaces. A reader who takes the number as 'rows removed because the source changed' has inverted it — the replace removes everything it is about to put back.

Every drift ratio is measured against the PRIOR completed run's `centreline_load.feature_count_filtered` (47363 on the last audited load), and on a first run — or any run whose prior-run read failed — the prior is null and the drift is 0 BY DEFINITION, not by measurement. `staleness.on_prior_run_error: "warn_row"` (LC-D4) makes the failed-read case VISIBLE as an additive row, so a 0 with a warning beside it is 'no baseline', never 'nothing moved'.

blind_spots.what: Geometry is validated for TYPE and validity, never for PLACE. A publisher that shipped the same ~47K well-formed LineStrings translated by a kilometre would pass every check here: the count is unchanged, nothing needs repair, nothing departs. Only the downstream proximity joins enrich_centreline runs would move, and nothing in this step reads them.

A single-member MultiLineString residue is a pinned DEFECT (LC-D8), not a silent pass: the extraction of a LineString member is counted at `centreline_geometry_collection_extracted` and the dropped remainder by `centreline_geometry_skipped_pct`. But because the counter is 0 in 8/8 measured runs, the residue has never been observed live — nothing here has actually exercised that arm.

decisions.what: The L25 INCLUDE/EXCLUDE feature-code sets, the `unknown_operator_review` sentinel and the FEDERAL drop are domain vocabulary kept in compute — NOT Rule 3 tunables.
decisions.why: They are code structure: which street classes exist is a fact about Toronto's data, not an operator knob, and an operator who could re-point the include set could silently redefine what a street is. The Rule 3 ledger externalizes only the six numeric thresholds it declares (LC-D3); promoting the sets to config would be declaring a phantom knob. Same disposition as the ravines classification sets.

decisions.what: `spec_version` stays the pinned '1.1' even though the consumer and the header may read otherwise.
decisions.why: enrich-centreline.js pins the producer contract version EXACTLY, and the sources chain HALTs on anything else. The pin is the contract; the document's number is documentation. Bumping it to match a header would look like tidying and would stop the chain — never bump it without a coordinated enrich_centreline change.

known_bad.what: LC-D14: the F-C1 preserve path emits `features_inserted: 0` while a prior load's ~47K rows remain in toronto_centreline, and enrich_centreline's assertCentrelineEnriched reads that field and will HALT. This is a known_bad until ④b flips the pin — the preserve is correct, the observable is not.

do_not_reflag.what: `centreline_count_drift_pct` and `centreline_geometry_skipped_pct` are declared `blocking: false`, so a FAIL verdict still exits 0.
do_not_reflag.why: Both are PINs, DO NOT FIX (plan D-8). The FAIL row is verdict-bearing and the write is genuinely skipped (both are scored at `when: "pre_write"`, so no transaction opens and toronto_centreline survives untouched) — but the run leaves `failed` with exit code 0, matching the legacy posture. Do not 'fix' this by making either check block: that is ④b's call, not a conversion defect.

how_to_investigate.what: A skip you did not expect: read `centreline_load_skipped` — the detail names WHICH gate ended the run. `content_hash` in the reason means the ZIP bytes are identical to the prior load and CKAN merely re-stamped last-modified (the daily-regen tier-2 case, the normal outcome). A validator reason (`unchanged_last_modified` / `unchanged_etag`) means the tier-1 HEAD gate fired and the 117 MB archive was never downloaded. Only CENTRELINE_FORCE_RELOAD=1 bypasses both.

A short table: walk the counters in order — `centreline_feature_count_raw` (every parsed record, measured 64385), then the L25 drops (`filtered_out_non_street` naming each `non_street` reason, `filtered_out_federal`), then `centreline_feature_count_filtered` (post-classify, post-dedupe: 47363). A gap between raw and filtered with `filtered_out_non_street: 0` is where a bad CENTREL2 or a null geometry landed — check `centreline_bad_centreline_id_count` and `centreline_null_geometry_count`.

limitations.what: LC-D17: null-geometry source records are counted by the LIBRARY before `shapeRecord` runs, whereas the legacy counted them AFTER the L25 classify — so `centreline_null_geometry_count` is measured at a different point in the pipeline than the pre-conversion counter. Same WARN posture, different ordering; 0 on run 1471 and 0 in the PRE capture, so the divergence is currently invisible in the numbers.
limitations.measured: LC-D17; a null-geometry record the L25 classify would have dropped is now visible to the count

fences.const: the F-C1 dual-mode empty-temp guard — first run + zero carried rows is a FAIL that aborts BEFORE any write; a later run + zero carried rows is a WARN with `on_warn: "skip_write"` that preserves toronto_centreline exactly as the prior run left it
fences.value: checks f_c1_empty_temp_guard_fired_first_run (FAIL, when:pre_write, conjunct ctx.prior == null) + f_c1_empty_temp_guard_fired (WARN, when:pre_write, on_warn:skip_write); the legacy reused ONE metric name for both arms, which is why the ids were split
fences.incident: Severity HIGH. On the later-run arm a WARN alone is not enough: the DELETE would open and empty the street network enrich_centreline joins against, so the check must REFUSE the write (skip_write), not merely flag it. The emit's `features_inserted: 0` on this path is the LC-D14 known_bad that HALTs enrich_centreline until ④b.

fences.const: the legacy ORDER guarantees: L7 count-drift and L8 geometry-skip are both scored at when:pre_write so their FAILs abort BEFORE the DELETE opens a transaction
fences.value: centreline_count_drift_pct (limit_from_config load_centreline_count_drift_fail_pct, default 0.5) + centreline_geometry_skipped_pct (limit_from_config load_centreline_invalid_geometry_fail_pct, default 0.05); order_guarantee blocks on both name Spec 62 §3.5's abort-before-withTransaction
fences.incident: Severity HIGH. Moving either check to a post_write seat would let a publisher error — half as many streets, or >5% unrepairable geometry — commit a DELETE-and-replace first and only then redden. The prior table would already be gone. The drift override CENTRELINE_ACCEPT_FEATURE_COUNT_DRIFT=1 enables execution and NEVER suppresses the FAIL row, so the abort still has to land pre-write.

fences.const: the tier-2 content-hash gate over a STREAMED md5 hash-through-to-disk — contentHashDecision + the re-emit of the prior block, and never a whole-buffer download or a whole-file read
fences.value: staleness.trigger[content_hash @ post_acquisition]; md5; the tier-2 skip still lands a COMPLETED row carrying the prior centreline_load block (DS4), and it is the gate CKAN's DAILY regeneration makes the normal outcome
fences.incident: Severity HIGH (commit 0b230472). Two failures in one commit: the 117 MB archive was buffered entirely into memory before hashing (Spec 43 §9.5 bans it — the same pattern on a 327 MB CSV is an OOM), and every metadata re-stamp by CKAN forced a full re-parse and ~47K no-op rows because nothing compared the bytes. Reverting either is invisible in the outputs, which is why the lock reads the code.

fences.const: the 3-attempt download — `attempts = 3` SPLITS into retries 2 (+1) with a zero backoff, and a genuine block fails all three
fences.value: execution.network.retries 2 (retries_from_config load_centreline_download_retries), retry_backoff_from_config load_centreline_download_retry_backoff_ms (0 = legacy: the loop sleeps never); the partial file is dropped between attempts
fences.incident: Severity MEDIUM. Fold IC-8 supersedes the plan's single-attempt wording: reading the descriptor for `attempts: 3` and calling the split a regression is the misread to avoid — CKAN/CDN drops large-file connections intermittently and the retry is what absorbs it. The legacy literal is `attempts = 3` (load-centreline.js:306-315); the seed defaults are byte-equal to it.
